newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-FULTON COUNTY STADIUM HOSTS ITS LAST GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-FULTON COUNTY STADIUM HOSTS ITS LAST GAME.

text.p: It has hosted an Olympics, the Beatles and Atlanta's first championship but Fulton County Stadium will always be known best as the house where Henry Aaron surpassed Babe Ruth's home run record.

On April 8, 1974, Aaron whacked career home run number 715 in Fulton County Stadium, which saw its last baseball game on Thursday as the Atlanta Braves hosted the New York Yankees in Game 5 of a World Series that has provided one last set of thrills.

The stadium, completed in 1965 at a cost of $18 million, will be replaced next year by a $200 million stadium that was also used as a venue for the Olympics earlier this summer. That facility is to be named after Ted Turner, the media mogul who owns the Braves and so much else.

The old stadium, never one of the major leagues' classics, was known as the "launching pad" for its friendliness to home run hitters. The original launcher was Yankees manager Joe Torre, a former Atlanta player and manager who hit the first regular-season homer here.

The Braves of Atlanta, descendants of the Boston and Milwaukee Braves, did not win a World Series until David Justice's homer and Tom Glavine's one-hit pitching snared the city's first championship in a 1-0 Game 6 here last year.

But this ballpark, while lacking all the history of a Yankee Stadium, has now seen four of the last five World Series, including one some fans consider the greatest of all time, 1991's epic seven-gamer in which four games were settled on the last pitch, five by one run and three in extra innings.
